says: In next/, this branch's new process.ack span tags itself with the reader's fab.process before its ledger turn runs, so the span sink files the child ledger.transaction span in the reader's job by its parent, but that child carries no fab.process of its own. P12's law that every record in a process's job names that process went red. Fixed in the same pull request: process.ack annotates every span inside it with the reader's process, as the brain already does for a process's own work.
proof: instance-records.integration.test.ts on this head: `expected false to be true` at line 875; a debug print showed the one record without fab.process was a ledger.transaction whose parent was process.ack. The same file on origin/main 27512b5f7, which has no process.ack: 13 of 13 passed. After the fix, 13 of 13 on this branch.
cost: A reader of one job's records finds a ledger turn that does not say whose it is, and the P12 law stays red on every full run.
